categories.main_business_segments: Clorox operates through four reportable segments: Health and Wellness (cleaning, disinfecting, and professional products), Household (bags and wraps, cat litter, grilling products), Lifestyle (food, water-filtration, and natural personal care), and International (products sold outside the U.S. across similar categories). These segments are organized by strategic business units and reflect the company's broad portfolio of consumer and professional brands.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Clorox leverages proprietary formulations and manufacturing processes for cleaning, disinfecting, and personal care products, including the use of sodium hypochlorite for bleach and advanced resin and non-woven fabric technologies for wipes and bags. The company is investing in digital transformation, including a new cloud-based ERP system and other digital technologies to enhance supply chain, innovation, and brand building capabilities.
categories.primary_customers_markets: The company primarily serves mass retailers, grocery outlets, warehouse clubs, dollar stores, home hardware centers, drug, pet, and military stores, as well as e-commerce channels and distributors. Walmart is the largest customer, accounting for 27% of net sales, and the five largest customers represent nearly half of total sales. Clorox also serves professional customers in institutional, janitorial, food-service, and healthcare markets.
categories.geographic_coverage: Clorox operates in approximately 25 countries or territories and sells products in about 100 markets worldwide. The U.S. is the dominant market, accounting for 86% of net sales in 2025, with the remaining 14% from international markets, including significant operations in Canada and Latin America.
categories.supply_chain_position: Clorox is primarily a downstream operator, manufacturing and marketing branded consumer and professional products that are sold through retail and distribution channels to end customers. The company sources raw materials from a global network of suppliers and manages its own manufacturing, distribution, and brand marketing.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The IGNITE strategy drives Clorox's focus on long-term, profitable growth through innovation, digital transformation, and sustainability. Key initiatives include investment in transformative technologies (ERP, digital commerce), product innovation (new flavors, scents, and formats), and portfolio evolution (divestitures and acquisitions). Sustainability, talent development, and operational resilience are also strategic priorities.
categories.revenue_model: Clorox generates revenue primarily through the sale of branded consumer and professional products to retailers, distributors, and direct-to-consumer channels. The company also sells to institutional and healthcare customers and receives some revenue from licensing and joint ventures, such as the Glad business with Procter & Gamble (winding down in 2026).
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Clorox faces intense competition from major multinational and national consumer products companies, as well as private label and store brands. Key competitors include Procter & Gamble, Reckitt, Colgate-Palmolive, and Kimberly-Clark. Clorox holds No. 1 or No. 2 market share positions in over 80% of its categories, emphasizing product performance, brand reputation, and innovation.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For fiscal year 2025, Clorox reported net sales of $7.1 billion and employed about 7,600 people worldwide. While net sales were essentially flat due to macroeconomic headwinds, the company grew market share and expanded gross margin, with diluted EPS increasing 190% year-over-year, reflecting recovery from prior-year disruptions and ongoing cost savings.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Clorox emphasizes trusted, high-performing brands with strong reputations for efficacy, safety, and sustainability. The company differentiates through innovation, brand equity, and a commitment to sustainability, with over 80% of sales from leading market share brands. Recognition for sustainability and management excellence further supports its value proposition to consumers and stakeholders.
